@graph.label: Bhaktapur District
@graph.description: Bhaktapur (Khwopa in Newari — 'city of devotees') was the last capital of the Malla dynasty. When the Shah kings unified Nepal in 1769, Bhaktapur was eclipsed politically but preserved culturally. Its narrow brick lanes, still paved with traditional handmade bricks, wind past 172 different temples and courtyards. Women dry their rice on bamboo mats; men shape pottery in the potters' square as they have for 800 years. Even today electricity was late to arrive, and the town retains an atmosphere that the other valley cities have largely lost to modernisation.
